{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

'''Panissa''' is a sort of Gibraltarian set pudding made with cooked chickpea flour. There is also an original [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] one, though what is referred to as panissa in Italy nowadays is more akin to the Gibraltarian [[Cookbook:Calentita|calentita]]. According to the original contributor, their grandmother always used to make panissa on the same day she made [[Cookbook:Minestra|Minestra]] as a light second course.

==Ingredients ==

* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Chickpea Flour|chickpea flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] for [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]]
* [[Cookbook:Mincing|Minced]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] (optional) 

==Procedure==

# Stir the chickpea flour into the 2 litres of lightly salted water over a moderate flame.
# Stir the mixture steadily in the same direction with a wooden spoon until you obtain a soft, lump-free paste.
# When the paste begins to pull away from the sides of the pot, turn it out into oiled wooden moulds, or spread it out about ¼ inch (½ cm) high on your work surface. Alternatively, pour the mixture into saucers. Make sure to dust the surface with parsley beforehand if you're including it. 
# Let the mixture cool and set.
# If you didn't use molds, cut the cooled mixture into 1 x 3-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (3 x 7 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) rectangles or into wedges.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the pieces in hot oil.

recipe.name: Deep Fried Chickpea Dough with Lemon (Panissa)

steps.text: Stir the chickpea flour into the 2 litres of lightly salted water over a moderate flame.
Stir the mixture steadily in the same direction with a wooden spoon until you obtain a soft, lump-free paste.

When the paste begins to pull away from the sides of the pot, turn it out into oiled wooden moulds, or spread it out about ¼ inch (½ cm) high on your work surface. Alternatively, pour the mixture into saucers. Make sure to dust the surface with parsley beforehand if you're including it.
Let the mixture cool and set.
If you didn't use molds, cut the cooled mixture into 1 x 3-inch (3 x 7 cm) rectangles or into wedges.
Fry the pieces in hot oil.
